tools.name: api_feedback_get-feedback
tools.description: Returns the submission (id, type, query, notes, created_at) plus its corrections, each with a review status in the public vocabulary: pending_review, needs_information, accepted, accepted_with_changes, rejected, withdrawn, applied, reverted (accepted means a reviewer agreed; applied means the change is live in the index). Only the submitting user's keys can read a submission; unknown ids and other users' submissions both return 404 (never 403). Required: feedback_id.

tools.name: api_feedback_submit-feedback
tools.description: Help shape Arcmira. Report a wrong result, request sources or capabilities, or tell us what would make your workflow more useful. To correct a result, attach corrections to the exact query you ran: pass the feedback type, the query object you sent, and optional per-item corrections. Public submissions are recorded for human review (status 'logged'); nothing is auto-applied. Read the review status back later via GET /v1/feedback/{feedback_id}. recommendations and channel_sponsors feedback types require a Pro+ plan; every other type needs read. monitor_alert feedback targets fired alerts: query carries monitor_id and/or tracker_id and/or alert_id, corrections target the alert id, and every referenced alert must belong to the caller (otherwise 404 alert_not_found). missed_alert corrections are expectations with nothing to target: omit the correction id and put { source_url, approximate_timestamp_seconds?, entity_id? } in suggested_change. delivery_issue corrections may carry { channel } in suggested_change. experience feedback says how a task went as a whole rather than correcting a result: it requires category and notes, refuses corrections (400 invalid_feedback_request), and needs no query. category and mcp_call_id, when sent, are recorded in the stored query. Optional: type, query, Idempotency-Key (plus 11 more). Returns the new FeedbackResponse.

params.name: type
params.description: Feedback type when omitted from the JSON body. Provide type in either location; the body takes precedence.

params.name: query
params.description: Query being reviewed when omitted from the JSON body. Body query fields override matching query-string fields.

params.name: Idempotency-Key
params.description: 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters (0x21 to 0x7E); anything else is 400 invalid_idempotency_key. Persist a unique key and the exact request before sending a logical mutation. A retry returns its stored response with Idempotency-Replayed: true. A changed intent under a finalized key returns 409 idempotency_conflict. Keys belong to the authenticated owner, credential and mutation domain. Current authorization still applies. Receipts have no general 24-hour expiry; signing-secret recovery alone expires after 24 hours or when the secret is displaced.

params.description: What kind of problem this is. Pass the window the rest of your answer uses: days=90 for a 90-day answer. The fixed 7, 30 and 90 day counts stay on every card. It counts the shows we index, not the whole internet, and it is a count, not a score. On a Pro+ plan the card also carries paid_vs_organic for the window; otherwise that field is absent and access names the gate. On a plan with a freshness gate, the window ends at the cutoff and the card carries freshness, unlock, and a note that says where results stop. A retry with the original Idempotency-Key recovers the same secret for up to 24 hours while it remains the current secret or the valid previous secret. An expired or displaced secret returns 409 idempotency_result_expired without rotating again. Reads do not expose the secret. Zero-downtime overlap: the previous secret remains valid until previous_secret_expires_at (24 hours); during the window every delivery carries an additional X-Arcmira-Signature-Previous header computed with the old secret over the same {timestamp}.{payload} string, so you can verify with either secret while you roll. After the window the old secret is dropped and the extra header disappears. Rotating again during the window replaces the previous secret and resets the window. Requires a configured webhook (webhook_url set); otherwise 409 with code webhook_not_configured. Auto-disable interplay: rotation resets webhook_failures but never re-enables a webhook that was auto-disabled after repeated failures; to resume delivery, also PATCH the monitor with notify_webhook: true. Requires the monitors:write scope. Required: id. Optional: Idempotency-Key.

tools.description: Starts the signup that ends in an account key, with no key and no login. Sends a 6 digit code to the address, valid for 10 minutes and 5 attempts, and answers 202 with the verify call. Sends are capped at 3 per address per hour, 10 per IP per hour, and 25 per client fingerprint per day; past a cap the response is 429 signup_send_limited with retry_after_seconds and an unlock whose action is this call. An address that already has an account gets a code too; verifying it mints a key on that account. Send { 'email': 'agent@example.com' }, with an optional 'src' naming the surface that sent you. Required: email. Optional: src. Returns the new SignupSentResponse. (public)

A wrong, expired, or spent code is 400 signup_code_invalid on param code, naming the attempts left; its unlock action is a new send. Send { 'email': 'agent@example.com', 'code': '482913' }. Required: code, email. Returns the new SignupVerifiedResponse. (public)

tools.name: transcript_search_search
tools.description: Search indexed YouTube and podcast transcripts for passages matching a word or phrase. Returns passage text, source metadata, publication dates, and timestamped watch links. Narrow to passages about an entity with `about`, or passages where a person speaks with `by`. Scope with `channel_ids` (or `channel`) and `entity_ids` (a person id filters to that person's appearances). Filter to sponsored, organic or mention passages with `kind`. Every filter takes ids, never names: resolve a name first with GET /v1/entities/resolve, or the call answers 400 id_required naming the parameter. Results carry names beside ids (filters.about, filters.by, chunk about and speakers_by). Use one topic per call. Search results include text on every plan within the plan's publication-date window. Explicitly requesting source=arcmira_premium on a plan without Premium transcripts is refused with filter_requires_paid. An after later than the plan's freshness gate is refused with freshness_requires_paid rather than widened. A window the gate cut carries freshness (delay_days, served_through), unlock, and a note that says where results on this plan stop. Uses 4 credits per chunk returned past the first 5. Every gate is a typed error whose error.unlock.url names the plan that lifts it; pass src=mcp-tool only from the Arcmira MCP server. Required: q. Optional: channel_ids, channel, entity_ids (plus 8 more).

params.name: q
params.description: One topic or phrase. Do not concatenate unrelated names; make one call per topic.

params.name: channel_ids
params.description: Comma-separated YouTube channel ids (UC...), at most 8. Pass every show in scope unless drilling into one. Ids only: a name answers 400 id_required. Resolve names first with GET /v1/entities/resolve.

params.name: channel
params.description: Alias of channel_ids for code-mode clients; the union of both is the scope.

params.name: entity_ids
params.description: Comma-separated entity ids (ent_{n}), at most 8. A person id filters to that person's appearances; a channel id widens channel_ids. Ids only: a name answers 400 id_required. Resolve names first with GET /v1/entities/resolve.

params.name: about
params.description: Comma-separated entity ids (ent_{n}), at most 8. Only passages about these entities: excerpt pins, exact-name mentions and ad verdicts. Ids only: a name answers 400 id_required. Resolve names first with GET /v1/entities/resolve.

params.name: by
params.description: Comma-separated person ids (ent_{n}), at most 8. Only passages where one of these people speaks the query words. A passage can include other speakers' lines; each line with a known speaker starts with that speaker's name. A non-person id is refused with invalid_query naming its type. Speaker labels cover a minority of shows; an empty result carries a note saying whether the person is labeled anywhere. Ids only: a name answers 400 id_required. Resolve names first with GET /v1/entities/resolve.

params.name: kind
params.description: Comma-separated passage classes: sponsored, organic, mention. Combine with about to read what was said about a brand in ad reads or in organic talk.

An ISO 8601 date (2026-09-01) or datetime with offset (2026-09-01T00:00:00Z), read in UTC. The window is half-open: after is inclusive, before is exclusive.

Each entry is a Premium transcript job with its processing and billing state, a `status_url` for the Premium transcript GET, and a `title` field (the video title, null when unknown). The scheduled reconciler advances requests; reading this list never dispatches work or changes billing. In-flight entries carry `eta_seconds` and `next_poll_seconds`. tools.name: transcripts_get
tools.description: Caption reads use 4 credits per started 15 minutes. quality=premium is one read. An owned transcript answers 200 ready at no charge. Otherwise this call starts a Premium transcript of the whole video, 300 credits per started 15 minutes, using credits from the account's plan first and then the account's on-demand budget up to its limit, and answers 202 pending with the job and Retry-After until the transcript is ready. Read again after Retry-After; repeated reads join the same job and never charge twice. When the last Premium transcript for the video failed, the read answers 200 state failed with the job and last_attempt and charges nothing; retry=true starts a new one. When the plan or the budget blocks, 403 paid_plan_required (with unlock) or 402 quota_exceeded or spend_limit_exceeded carries the price in quote and the limit it met in limit, and nothing is charged. A default-premium account with nothing owned reads captions with a note. On captions, start and end set the billed window: 4 credits per started 15 minutes of end minus start. On Premium they only trim the returned content, and the charge is the whole video. language selects caption tracks, timestamps=false returns paragraphs. Premium lines carry speaker and index, and the body carries speakers and revision. language picks the language: language= returns the base transcript (base_language), and a language the transcript is not in returns it translated, line for line with the same timestamps and speakers. Captions offer only the languages YouTube makes available for the video (translation_languages), billed as a caption read; any other language is Premium: an owned Premium transcript in another language costs the Premium rate once per account and language. Required: video_id. Optional: quality, language, timestamps (plus 5 more).

params.name: video_id
params.description: YouTube video id, 11 characters.

params.name: quality
params.description: captions reads creator or automatic captions at 4 credits per started 15 minutes. premium is one read. An owned transcript returns 200 state ready at no charge. Otherwise the read starts a Premium transcript of the whole video, 300 credits per started 15 minutes, using credits from the account's plan first and then the account's on-demand budget up to its limit, and returns 202 state pending with the job until it is ready. When the last Premium transcript for the video failed it answers 200 state failed and starts a new one only with retry=true. 402 quota_exceeded or spend_limit_exceeded and 403 paid_plan_required carry the price in quote. It never substitutes captions. Default captions unless changed in account settings.

params.name: language
params.description: The language to read the transcript in, as a code (e.g. 'es') or a comma-separated priority list of at most 5 (e.g. 'de,en'); asr picks the first automatic caption track and asr- a specific one. Every transcript has a base language, base_language in the response: the language of the original caption track, or the language a Premium transcript was spoken and transcribed in. language= with no value returns the base transcript; so does a code in the base language. Omitted, the account default applies (en unless changed), falling back to the base transcript. When no code in the list matches, the transcript is translated into the first code, line for line with the same timestamps and speakers. Captions translate only into the languages YouTube makes available for the video (translation_languages in the response, or GET /v1/videos/{video_id}/captions), billed as a caption read of the window, 4 credits per started 15 minutes; any other code answers 400 invalid_query naming the Premium read. On a Premium transcript the account owns, each other language costs the Premium rate, 300 credits per started 15 minutes, once per account and language, and is free after that. While a translation runs the read answers 503 transcript_fetching with Retry-After and progress, and charges nothing. languages[] lists every caption track the video offers.

params.name: timestamps
params.description: false returns paragraphs[] of { start, text, speaker? } instead of lines[], for reading rather than citing. Default true.

params.name: start
params.description: Window start in seconds from the beginning of the video. Send start and end together. On captions the window bills only its own started 15-minute blocks; on Premium it trims the returned content. An explicit Premium read is charged for the whole video from the account's plan credits and then its on-demand budget; a window does not reduce that charge.

params.name: end
params.description: Window end in seconds, greater than start and no greater than the video duration. Send start and end together.

params.name: retry
params.description: Premium only; captions with retry=true returns invalid_query. When the last Premium transcript for this video failed, a read answers 200 state failed with the job and last_attempt and charges nothing; retry=true starts a new one under the same quote, budget and one-job-per-video rules as the first read. While that refund is still settling (job.status refund_pending) even retry=true answers state failed. Without a failed job it changes nothing.

params.name: refresh
params.description: Captions only; Premium with refresh=true returns invalid_query. Refetch the caption track from YouTube instead of serving the stored copy. Available only for videos outside our index; a pipeline-owned video refuses it with invalid_query.

params.name: src
params.description: The surface making this call.

tools.name: transcripts_quote_transcription
tools.description: Optional free quote: what a Premium read of this video would use right now, as credits (charge; quote.rows restates it in rows, and a row is 4 credits), where the credits would come from, and max_on_demand_cents, the on-demand budget the read would need beyond the plan's credits within the account limit. It does not reserve credits or budget and does not start a transcript. A video with no known duration, or one past the 12 hour cap, answers 400 invalid_query with param video_id. Required: video_id. Returns the PremiumQuote.

params.name: video_id
params.description: YouTube video id, 11 characters.
